pending_prompt:
Read .claude/PROJECT_BRIEF.md for context. Phase 0 (skeleton setup) is done. Before I
deploy to Render, verify and finalize everything so both local development and
production deploy work without issues on the first try.

Do the following, in order:

1. Run `bin/rails server` locally and confirm the app actually boots with no errors.
   Fix anything that doesn't.

2. Double-check config/database.yml:
   - development and test should work with local Postgres out of the box
   - production must read from ENV["DATABASE_URL"], since that's what Render injects
     automatically when I attach a Postgres instance

3. Double-check config/master.key and config/credentials.yml.enc exist and are set up
   correctly. Confirm config/master.key is in .gitignore (it must NEVER be committed).
   Print the exact contents of config/master.key to the terminal so I can copy it —
   I need to paste this into Render's RAILS_MASTER_KEY environment variable myself.

4. Confirm config/environments/production.rb has:
   - config.force_ssl = true
   - config.log_level appropriate for production (:info, not :debug)
   - config.assets.compile = false
   - Proper handling for serving static files if Render doesn't use a separate CDN/proxy
     (config.public_file_server.enabled should be true unless we're offloading to
     something else)

5. Confirm the Gemfile has puma configured correctly for production, and check
   config/puma.rb for a reasonable WEB_CONCURRENCY / thread setup that works within
   Render's free-tier instance limits (512MB RAM, low CPU) — don't over-provision
   worker processes.

6. Add a .gitignore check: confirm config/master.key, .env, /tmp, /log, /storage
   (if using local disk for ActiveStorage in dev) are all ignored. .agent-logs/ must
   NOT be ignored — confirm it's still tracked.

7. Create or verify render.yaml at the repo root, or if you determine manual dashboard
   setup is more reliable, skip the file and instead give me the exact build command
   and start command to paste into Render's dashboard.

8. Run `bundle exec rspec` or `rails test` (whichever the app is using) to confirm
   there are no failing tests from the skeleton setup, even if it's just the default
   generated tests.

9. Stage and commit everything with a clear commit message describing this as the
   finalized, deploy-ready skeleton. Do NOT commit config/master.key or any secrets.
   Push to the GitHub remote.

10. Give me a final numbered checklist, in order, of exactly what I need to do manually
    in the Render dashboard: signing up, connecting the GitHub repo, creating the
    Postgres instance (same region as the web service), and which environment
    variables to set (DATABASE_URL is automatic from Render's Postgres add-on link,
    but RAILS_MASTER_KEY needs to be pasted in manually — remind me to use the value
    printed in step 3).

Stop after step 10 and wait for me to confirm the app is live on Render.
